output.methodChoice: Competing hypotheses (D), because several rival explanations needed to be told apart by a few discriminating data cuts.
output.brief: The rise is not mainly a handler problem. Since 1 September, Corvane's tags printed on the new Fennick stock fail automatic reading about 12% of the time, against 1.5% before. Transfer tags and Pelion tags, handled by the same crews and the same readers, stay at about 1.3–1.4%. Pelion's mishandling rate did not rise under the same Tessaly crew pool. The extra bags go to the manual encode desk, wait about 30 minutes, and reach the lateral after it closes. In the 14–16 October test, counter tags on old Brackwater stock failed at 1.6% while kiosk tags on Fennick failed at 12.1% on the same days. I am quite sure the tag stock, or how the printers handle it, is the cause. I cannot yet say whether the stock is defective or the printer heat setting is wrong. Do not send the breach notice or withhold the fee, because that would punish the wrong party. Switch counters and kiosks back to the Brackwater stock held in stores now (about five weeks' supply, contract valid to 31 Dec). Then test Fennick stock at the correct printer settings before making any claim against the supplier. Asking the airport for an extra encode workstation in the evening is a reasonable stopgap.
